title: Slow-Cooker Butter Chicken
subtitle: Creamy tomato-spiced chicken in the slow cooker
excerpt: Chicken thighs cooked all day in a gently spiced tomato and cream sauce. The sauce is blended at the end for the characteristic smooth texture. Richer and more forgiving than the stovetop version.

recipe.sourceNotes: Butter chicken (murgh makhani) was developed at the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s by Kundan Lal Gujral, who used leftover tandoori chicken in a tomato and butter sauce. The British-adapted version is milder, creamier, and uses chicken cooked directly in the sauce rather than tandoor-cooked chicken added to it. The slow cooker method produces a very tender, moist result because the chicken absorbs the sauce during the long cooking time.

content.text: The cream and butter go in at the end, after the main cooking is done, so they do not split during the long simmer. Blend the sauce before adding the cream for the smooth, velvety texture characteristic of the dish. A stick blender works directly in the slow cooker pot.

Put the chicken thighs, onion, garlic, ginger, garam masala, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chilli powder, tomato puree, and tinned tomatoes into the slow cooker. Season with salt. Stir to combine. Cook on LOW for 5 to 6 hours or HIGH for 3 hours.
Remove the chicken thighs and shred roughly with two forks, or leave whole if preferred.
Blend the sauce in the slow cooker pot with a stick blender until smooth. Stir in the cream and butter. Return the chicken to the pot. Taste and season.
Serve with basmati rice and naan, scattered with coriander.
